newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Wednesday and traders said early-maturing contracts were actively traded due to enlarged volume on the domestic A share markets.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 10.90 percent from 11.05 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover fell to 4.72 million lots from 5.28 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The early-maturing contracts traded actively today due to active trading on the A share markets," one trader said.
Traders believe the repo rates will continue to fall due to expected falls on the A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down with big institutions selling to raise money to cope with an annual finance audit by the central bank, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell slightly to 117.05 yuan from 117.08.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.18 million lots from 1.31 million.
Traders said the spot contracts would continue to fall with institutions needing money to settle accounts at the year-end.
